name: Fingernail Detail Analysis
description: Analyzes fingernail texture, lunula, and cuticle details — AI often generates amorphous or inconsistent nail structures.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated content by analyzing the anatomical correctness and detail fidelity of fingernails, which are consistently problematic for generative models:

1. **Nail Plate Geometry Validation**: Real fingernails have well-defined geometric properties — the nail plate is a smooth, gently convex surface with consistent curvature (radius 8–15 mm), aspect ratio (width:length approximately 1:1.2–1:1.5), and symmetric shape about the longitudinal axis. The method extracts nail region proposals using hand pose estimation (MediaPipe), then validates nail geometry: (a) nail boundary smoothness via Fourier descriptor analysis — real nails have smooth contours dominated by low-frequency components, (b) bilateral symmetry — real nails are nearly symmetric, with asymmetry index < 0.1, (c) convexity — the nail surface should be uniformly convex without concavities. AI-generated nails frequently exhibit irregular boundaries, asymmetric shapes, incorrect aspect ratios, or merged/extra nails on a single finger.

2. **Lunula and Cuticle Structure Analysis**: The lunula (half-moon shaped lighter area at the nail base) has specific anatomical properties: it appears at the proximal end, has a crescent shape, is lighter than the surrounding nail plate (higher L* value in L*a*b* space), and is most prominent on thumbs with decreasing visibility toward the pinky. The cuticle forms a thin, uniform border along the proximal nail fold. The method validates lunula presence, shape, color, and position using a trained segmentation model. AI generators frequently omit the lunula entirely, place it incorrectly, generate it with wrong color, or merge it with the cuticle — these errors are subtle but anatomically impossible.

3. **Nail Surface Texture Analysis**: Real nail plates exhibit characteristic surface texture — fine longitudinal ridges (spacing 0.1–0.3 mm) running from cuticle to free edge, with ridge prominence increasing with age. The method analyzes this texture using: (a) directional Gabor filters to detect ridge orientation — should be predominantly longitudinal, (b) ridge spacing regularity — measured via autocorrelation, (c) specular reflection pattern — the nail surface produces elongated specular highlights aligned with the longitudinal ridges. AI-generated nails typically show either smooth, textureless surfaces (lacking ridges entirely) or incorrect texture patterns (non-longitudinal, irregular spacing, or painted-on appearance).

4. **Cross-Finger Consistency and Hand Context**: On a real hand, all visible fingernails share consistent properties: similar nail bed color, compatible size gradation (thumb largest, pinky smallest), consistent grooming state (all trimmed or all grown), and same polish/natural state. The method validates cross-finger consistency and checks contextual plausibility: nail size proportional to finger width, nail orientation matching finger direction, and proper spatial arrangement. AI generators frequently produce hands where different fingers have incompatible nail sizes, colors, or states — one nail may appear polished while others are natural, or nail sizes may not follow the anatomical gradation.
parameters:
Hand detection: MediaPipe hand pose (21 landmarks)
Nail segmentation: U-Net trained on nail datasets
Geometry validation: Fourier descriptors up to 10th harmonic
Symmetry threshold: asymmetry index < 0.1
Lunula detection: separate semantic segmentation
Ridge analysis: Gabor filters (0°, 15°, 30° orientations)
Ridge spacing: 0.1–0.3 mm expected range
Minimum nail resolution: 32×32 pixels per nail
Cross-finger consistency: pairwise color ΔE < 5 in L*a*b*
accuracy: 79–88% accuracy detecting AI-generated hands via nail analysis. Nail geometry validation achieves AUC of 0.85 for StyleGAN and Midjourney outputs. Lunula analysis provides F1-score of 0.82. Cross-finger consistency is the strongest individual signal (AUC 0.87). Performance requires sufficient hand resolution and is strongest for close-up hand views.
source: Farid, H. (2022). Creating, Using, Misusing, and Detecting Deep Fakes. Journal of Online Trust and Safety, 1(4), 1–33.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated imagery through hand and nail analysis. Supplementary signal for deepfake detection in full-body video. Quality assessment of AI image generators. Forensic analysis of close-up hand images in suspected AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Targets well-known weakness of current AI generators — hands and nails
• Multiple independent signals (geometry, lunula, texture, cross-finger consistency)
• Lunula and ridge analysis exploit anatomical details rarely modeled by generators
• Works as strong supplementary signal even when face analysis is inconclusive
• Cross-finger consistency check is simple but highly discriminative
limitations:
• Requires hands to be visible and at sufficient resolution
• Nail polish, artificial nails, and nail art reduce anatomical signal availability
• Improving generator quality (DALL-E 3, Midjourney v5+) produces better hands
• Small or distant hands in video lack sufficient pixel detail
• Cultural variations in nail grooming affect baseline expectations
